items.name: TrendForce press release Fri 27 Nov 'Limited demand visibility and growing supply chain caution heighten risk of DRAM contract price declines in 2028': since early 4Q26 supply-chain participants have been reassessing 2027 and 2028 production and sales plans, 'slightly slowing overall DRAM procurement'; BASE CASE - conventional DRAM contract-price increases narrow progressively through 2027, potentially levelling off in 2H27, then fall across ALL product categories from 1Q28 as shortages ease if server-shipment growth slows; BEAR CASE - server-shipment growth decelerates as early as 2027, contract prices reverse and decline from 4Q27 with declines widening in 2028, server OEMs scale back procurement and inventories are cut across the chain; named drivers: a more cautious stance toward domestic US data-centre development after the midterms, power-supply constraints reshaping 2028 DC construction demand, 'possible changes to NVIDIA's financing support for neocloud providers' that could indirectly reduce server procurement and DRAM demand, Chinese CSPs scaling back server DRAM demand since early 4Q26 (North American CSPs have 'largely absorbed' the freed supply), consumer-electronics makers with limited capacity to absorb further price rises, and the new BIS rules (remote-access licensing for DCs serving Chinese firms; foundry approval for advanced-node chips to Chinese IC designers) weighing on Asian DRAM demand; bear-case extras: neocloud consolidation, reduced investment, stricter BIS controls; supply: 'strong' global DRAM bit growth 2026-2028 from new capacity and node migration (no percentages); no HBM, NAND, LTA or inventory-level figures; no quarterly price percentages. Same day: 247wallst - 'no memory order cuts reported', MU >75% of FY27 committed (30 Sep call), SNDK NBM visibility beyond FY2030, WDC 'up to 2030, 2031' across its top seven customers; the memory names rallied through the release (MU +7.6%, SNDK +16%, SK hynix ADR +6% morning)
items.headline: TrendForce (27 Nov): DRAM contract-price rises narrow through 2027 and turn to declines from 1Q28 (bear case 4Q27) - names post-midterm US DC caution, 2028 power limits, possible changes to Nvidia's neocloud financing support and Chinese CSP cutbacks since early 4Q26; memory stocks rallied anyway
items.claim: Two days after cutting its 2027 DRAM revenue forecast, TrendForce now puts a date on the price turn (1Q28 base, 4Q27 bear) and lists Nvidia's neocloud financing support and US data-centre deliverability (midterms, power) alongside Chinese CSP cutbacks as the reasons demand visibility has shortened - the forecaster is tying memory pricing to the AI-credit channel, not just to supply growth.
items.candidate_dial: F1 memory LTA / memory-no-surface (no renegotiation - the release does not mention LTAs, and 247wallst confirms no order cuts and >75% FY27 committed at Micron; the new content is (i) a dated price-turn (1Q28 base / 4Q27 bear) and (ii) the explicit citation of Nvidia neocloud-financing changes and post-midterm DC caution as demand-visibility risks - a forecaster linking the memory cycle to the C2-capex/credit fuse; the equity response (+6-16%) says the market read it as already priced after the 30-48% monthly drawdowns) / B2-capex (secondary)
items.source: TrendForce press center 'Limited Demand Visibility and Growing Supply Chain Caution Heighten Risk of DRAM Contract Price Declines in 2028, Says TrendForce' (27 Nov 2026); 24/7 Wall St 'SanDisk jumps 10% as investors return to beaten-down memory stocks; Micron and SK hynix rise 6% despite TrendForce DRAM warning' (27 Nov 08:58 ET)

items.name: Semafor (Wed 26 Nov, people familiar; relayed Benzinga/AOL 27 Nov 05:33Z and Pivot News 27 Nov via aiweekly): Citigroup and JPMorgan are among banks quietly marketing portfolios of AI-related loans, including data-centre loans, to outside investors to offload some exposure - some structured as synthetic risk transfers (loans stay on balance sheet, loss risk shifts to investors), pitched quietly to protect borrower relationships; Semafor: heavy AI debt issuance has 'crowded out' Treasuries and some investors feel 'tapped out'; some banks are simultaneously preparing to take on MORE AI lending; Citi declined comment, JPM no response; no loans, amounts, buyers or pricing identified in any relay; same day Bloomberg (refused host): BBVA weighs an SRT to hedge about EUR 500m (USD 547m) of data-centre loans ('considering', not done - FourWeekMBA relay); and the BoE FSR, per FourWeekMBA citing Bloomberg, puts the big cloud companies' total potential AI exposure at 'just over USD 4 trillion' including off-balance-sheet commitments, calling AI financing 'increasingly complex, circular and opaque' (figure relay-attributed; FSR PDF not read; the ai.info and financialmarkets.com relays carry no such number). Companion 27 Nov detail on the Asian DC-loan freeze (techtimes, Bloomberg-sourced): Citi and JPMorgan reportedly added an export-control DEFAULT CLAUSE to Bridge Data Centres' upsized USD 6.6bn loan (each had held USD 120.28m of Bridge's earlier 2.8bn facility; clause wording not public), DBS is lead arranger on the frozen USD 480m Aolani loan (declined comment), Standard Chartered launched a broad review of data-centre clients, Digital Halo's Malaysian site serves Alibaba (one bank passed on the fully underwritten 372m, others 'asking more questions'), UOB ~USD 1bn SRT not final, DayOne's listing paused with a BlackRock-led consortium weighing a LOWER bid; 'no cancelled deals are reported'
items.headline: Semafor: Citi and JPMorgan quietly shopping AI-loan portfolios (some via SRTs) as AI issuance 'crowds out' Treasuries and investors feel 'tapped out'; Bloomberg: BBVA weighs a EUR 500m DC-loan SRT; Citi/JPM add an export-control default clause to Bridge DC's USD 6.6bn; BlackRock group weighs a lower DayOne bid
items.claim: The bank-side mirror of the Asian loan freeze and the BoE's 'circular and opaque' warning: the two largest US AI-infrastructure lenders are now distributing or hedging exposure they recently underwrote, and adding export-control default triggers to new Asian DC loans, while the exit price for a Chinese-tenant DC platform (DayOne) is being marked down - risk is being moved and repriced, not yet pulled.
items.candidate_dial: A-debt / D3 private credit (lender-withdrawal signal from the originating banks themselves - but no size, buyer or price printed, so unscoreable as a 'pulled deal'; the orchestrator's test: whether the SRT/portfolio sales clear (banks keep lending, risk moves to insurers/private credit - the BoE's 'harder to see' outcome) or stall (banks cut new AI commitments - the demand-side fuse). The Bridge default clause is the first printed instance of export-control risk being written into AI-DC loan covenants; the DayOne 'lower bid' is the first printed markdown of an Asian DC asset.
